clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying the orchard: within months, June became homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily; Walter worked from dark to dark and grew distant from June; Glen got into fights at school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees. By September 1953, when June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, the period settles.

clusters.name: The orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: within months, Walter drank heavily most nights; Walter and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened; Nora began wetting the bed again in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working. By October 1969, when Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, the period settles.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within months, Glen sat out in the truck for hours most of that year; Glen and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and said little to her mother; Walter drank again after six years off it in December 1975. By June 1976, when Nora was eating again and made the track team, the period settles.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990: within months, Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Sam took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Sam rowed most nights; Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side. By August 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, the period settles.
